subject.title: [Feature Request] ACP Session Skill Context Injection

question: Should `sessions_spawn(runtime: "acp")` gain an OpenClaw skill-context injection contract, and which selection modes, prompt layer, redaction, audit metadata, and resume semantics are allowed?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the change crosses a core session/security boundary and overlaps Codex-native skill behavior, so automation should not choose the permanent API and prompt contract.

options.title: Design explicit contract first
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers specify explicit skill selection, redaction/audit metadata, prompt layer, resume behavior, and Codex/native parity before implementation.

options.title: Limit to explicit skill ids
options.body: Scope the first implementation to a per-call explicit `skills` selector and defer automatic/default injection until observability and privacy behavior are proven.

options.title: Decline core injection
options.body: Keep ACP harnesses isolated from OpenClaw-rendered skill content and direct users to harness-native skills, MCP, or plugin workflows instead.

recommendation.title: Design explicit contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers specify explicit skill selection, redaction/audit metadata, prompt layer, resume behavior, and Codex/native parity before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the ACP runtime/control-plane surface that the requested contract would extend.
